**featureMSEA** (Feature-based Metabolite Set Enrichment Analysis) is a powerful method for interpreting metabolomics data. Unlike conventional over-representation analysis, featureMSEA operates directly on metabolic features — including unannotated ones — to identify enriched metabolic pathways without requiring a hard annotation cutoff.

```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(
  echo    = TRUE,
  warning = FALSE,
  message = FALSE,
  fig.align = "center",
  out.width = "90%"
)
```

## What is featureMSEA? {-}

featureMSEA extends the classic Gene Set Enrichment Analysis (GSEA) framework to metabolomics. It ranks all detected metabolic features by a signal statistic (e.g., fold-change × significance) and evaluates whether features assigned to a given pathway are non-randomly distributed toward the top or bottom of that ranked list.

**Key advantages:**

```{=html}
<div class="feature-grid">
  <div class="feature-card">
    <span class="feature-label">Flexible input</span>
    <strong>Works with unannotated features</strong>
    <p>No strict annotation cutoff is required before pathway-level analysis.</p>
  </div>
  <div class="feature-card">
    <span class="feature-label">Databases</span>
    <strong>Multiple pathway resources</strong>
    <p>Supports KEGG, HMDB, iMETpD, Reactome, and WikiPathways workflows.</p>
  </div>
  <div class="feature-card">
    <span class="feature-label">Interpretation</span>
    <strong>LLM-assisted evaluation</strong>
    <p>Add optional AI-guided biological review for enriched pathways.</p>
  </div>
</div>
```

- Works with **unannotated features** — no strict annotation cutoff required
- Supports **multiple pathway databases**: KEGG, HMDB, iMETpD, Reactome, WikiPathways
- Integrates with **LLM-based biological evaluation** for AI-assisted interpretation
- Fully integrated into the **TidyMass Shiny** web interface

## Quick start {-}

The featureMSEA workflow consists of three main steps:

| Step | Description |
|------|-------------|
| **Step 1** | Metabolite annotation (MS1-based) |
| **Step 2** | Pathway enrichment analysis |
| **Step 3** | LLM evaluation *(optional)* |

To get started, see [Installation] for setup instructions, then follow the [Analysis Workflow] chapter.
